Patterns

How components combine for common jobs. Each is shown working in index.html.

A product's page

The parts of a page that says what something is and why to use it, in order. Take only those you have something true to put in.

  1. An announcement, if there's news (phase banner), dismissible.
  2. The site header with the page's one action, which stays in the bar on a phone (site header).
  3. The hero: a plain claim, a lede, two actions, and the real thing, not a picture of a feeling: a code sample (code) or the product itself.
  4. Who uses it (logo wall) and the figures (stats), each said with what it counts.
  5. What it does: feature tabs, each a name, a line, and a sample of it working.
  6. What people say (quotes), with their permission.
  7. Questions and answers (below).
  8. A call to action (call to action), once, at the end.

Each band is a section with an eyebrow and a heading written as a claim (writing). A long document has on this page beside it instead.

Questions and answers

The questions people ask before they start, answered on the page.

  • One disclosure per question, in a .al-disclosure-group, under a heading ("Questions"). The summary is the question as people would ask it; the answer is a short paragraph, with a link to the page that says more.
  • Order them by how often they're asked. Six to ten; past that, a help page.
  • Keep the answer in the page (<details>), so find-in-page and search engines reach it.

Ask, check, confirm

For anything sent, or hard to take back.

  1. Ask. One form, novalidate, checked on submit with js/validate.js: an error summary, inline errors, and "Error: " in the page title.
  2. Check. A summary list of the answers, each with a Change link that returns to the field with the answer kept.
  3. Confirm. A confirmation with what happens next. Disable the send action once pressed.

Never put answers in the address (no GET forms for personal data). Move focus to each step's heading or panel as it appears.

Pending changes

See save state.

  • Keep the saved value (the baseline) apart from the draft.
  • Number each edit. A save that completes marks "Saved" only if no edit has happened since it started; otherwise the state stays "Unsaved changes".
  • Ignore responses that arrive out of order.
  • Discard returns to the baseline and offers Undo, which restores the exact draft that was discarded.
  • On failure, keep the draft, say it couldn't save, and offer Retry, which saves the current draft.
  • Figures worked out from the value are marked stale until the latest calculation returns; an older result never clears the stale mark.

Optimistic changes and rollback

Do the change at once with Undo. If the server refuses, put the thing back where it was, mark it, say why in words, and offer Retry. Move focus to Retry.

Destructive changes

If it can be undone, do it and offer Undo. If it can't, use a dialog: name the thing and what goes with it, give the safer action first focus, and, for the most serious cases, ask for a typed confirmation that is checked before the dialog can close. Return focus to the trigger afterwards.

Empty, loading, error and offline

  • Empty: why there's nothing, and the next action (empty state).
  • Loading: progress where the work happens (loading); keep the layout stable.
  • Error: what failed, in words, what was kept, and Retry.
  • Offline: say changes are kept on this device and will be sent when the connection returns, only if that's true; otherwise say they can't be saved yet.
